title: Westbrook School Committee — Regular Meeting

fields.Location: Westbrook High School (Room 114), 125 Stroudwater St. (Hybrid via Zoom)

note: This summary highlights the meeting's key discussions and decisions, with direct quotes and timestamps for verification — it is not a substitute for watching the full meeting. All seven members were present. The committee adopted a state-required policy on immigration enforcement at schools and tabled the Siemens energy study after learning a funding deadline had passed. The vote to change the agenda order was counted at five in favor; every other vote was unanimous. Summarization necessarily condenses and selects; for complete context, nuance, and anything not covered, watch the full video at the link above. (Produced by: WestbrookCurrents.com)
attendance: Present: Chair Andrea Mancuso, Vice Chair Katy Rice, Allison Brunette, Erin Cavallaro, Noreen Poitras, Brooke Reed, Dr. Flynn Ross. Student representatives Jamila Mohamed Ahmed and Schuyler Stevenson also attended and gave advisory votes.

blocks.x: Opening & Procedural Record
Call to Order, Roll Call & Minutes
Discussion Summary
Chair Andrea Mancuso opened the meeting. All seven members and both student representatives answered the roll call.
Dr. Peter Lancia, the Superintendent, added one hire to the agenda [1:29]. Jesse Goodwin is the new K-12 library professional learning community leader, with $1,500 in extra pay (a stipend).
The committee approved the Oct. 14 minutes [2:01]. No one from the public spoke during the first public comment period, which was for agenda items only.
Key Decisions
Oct. 14 minutes approved. Moved by Erin Cavallaro, seconded by Dr. Flynn Ross. All seven members voted yes; the two student representatives gave advisory yes votes.
Superintendent's Report
Fall Music and Athletics
Discussion Summary
Music Director Suzanne Proulx read notes about the high school marching band and color guard. They earned their 15th gold medal and placed second at the New England Championships at Harvard Stadium.
Athletic Director Campbell gave the fall sports report [5:28]. He said this season brought fewer trophies but many lessons in character. Highlights he named:
Football went 3–5 in the regular season and kept the River Bowl trophy against Gorham for a second year.
Golfer Luke Rice, a sophomore, was the first Westbrook golfer in five years to qualify for the state championship. He finished 50th.
Runner Ezra Burke qualified for the cross-country state meet and finished 60th of 110.
Boys soccer went 9–5. It lost a home playoff game on the 30th penalty kick, after about four and a half hours of play.
Girls soccer went 7–6–1, one of its best records in about a decade.
Girls volleyball, under a first-year coach, lost a quarterfinal to Washington Academy, the defending Class B champion.
Campbell said some girls soccer players were targeted online this fall. The team chose to protest at its game at Windham. He praised how the players supported one another.
District News and Staffing
Discussion Summary
Dr. Lancia thanked the transportation and nutrition departments for a “Stuff a Bus” food drive at Hannaford. Food and money raised go to school pantries and Thanksgiving baskets.
High school students took 646 rides on the Metro bus from Nov. 1 to 12. Boardings topped 100 on three days. He said attendance is improving in every high school grade.
He listed open jobs [20:00]:
Special education: 12 education technician openings, two teachers, two speech-language pathologists and one director.
Transportation: two bus drivers and one bus aide.
Two noon duty aides and one school nutrition helper.
Substitutes, including long-term substitutes. He said this is the first full year of Maine's paid family and medical leave program, and many staff are taking leave.

Other news: Westbrook Adult Education met all four state performance targets for a second year. The Westbrook Regional Vocational Center had its first state accreditation visit. School nutrition won a $240,226 national grant to add student-designed, scratch-cooked protein entrées. An update on the district's improvement goals was moved to December.
Chair, Student and Committee Reports
Chair's Report
Discussion Summary
Chair Mancuso said school leaders met with Mayor David Morse, City staff, Councilor Brian McCambridge and the Council's finance chair. Siemens presented its energy work at that meeting.

A joint meeting with the City Council is tentatively set for Jan. 4, 2027. Teacher contract talks start in the next few weeks, with Erin Cavallaro filling in for Katy Rice on the team. The committee also plans listening sessions for school staff.
Cavallaro reported on the Maine School Boards Association's annual meeting [30:19]. She attended as Westbrook's delegate. Every resolution passed as proposed.
Student Representatives
Discussion Summary

Student representative Schuyler Stevenson shared a student survey. The survey asked about the locked phone pouches used at the high school [35:51]. Of 153 students who answered, 48.4% called them a bad thing, 41.8% didn't care and 9.8% called them a good thing. Stevenson said most students want access to their phones during the day.
Jamila Mohamed Ahmed reported news from Congin School, Westbrook Middle School and Saccarappa School.
Finance Committee Report
Discussion Summary
Noreen Poitras reported on the Nov. 4 Finance Committee meeting:
Pay changes from the new support staff contract are being made; the rest should be caught up by the next payroll.
Pre-K is in deficit until a state reimbursement arrives.
Substitute costs are running high. Staff will look at whether the state's paid leave program is a cause.
Electricity costs are high at the middle school. Asked why, a speaker said its solar panels came online later than budgeted [51:28].
Two capital projects ran over budget. Both come back later in the meeting (items 12.6 and 12.7).

School nutrition costs are rising faster than its federal reimbursement, which went up about 3%. Dr. Lancia said the program hasn't needed general fund support for about five years. In earlier years that support was about $75,000 to $100,000. He said a request could come in the fiscal year 2028 budget [50:14].
Educational Programs Committee Report
Discussion Summary

Vice Chair Katy Rice said Great Schools Partnership is leading a review of the whole special education program. Staff sessions and surveys are under way, and parents will be surveyed and invited to meetings. A report is hoped for in January.

A new technology task force is looking at how the district uses technology, including artificial intelligence. Members noted the district can't block Google's AI tool from students, because the schools use Google.
Policy Committee Report
Discussion Summary
Cavallaro reported on the Oct. 28 Policy Committee meeting:
New policy KLGC (the policy's file code), on immigration enforcement at schools, came to this meeting for a vote (see item 12.2).
Changes to the public comment policy are with the district's lawyers. She cited an April federal court case involving the Augusta Board of Education and free speech concerns.
After discussing vandalism at the middle and high schools, the committee decided not to propose a new policy. School leaders will handle it.
Policies on school resource officers go back to district leaders for review.
She proposed a subcommittee to review technology policies, including artificial intelligence, student data privacy and screen time.
The Policy Committee will meet Dec. 16 at 5 PM at Central Office, in the Facilities Committee's usual slot.
Facilities Committee Report
Discussion Summary

Brooke Reed said the committee toured the high school. Needs it saw include field drainage, the track, bleachers, tennis courts, parking and old classroom furniture. It also ranked projects in the capital improvement plan, the long-term list of big building projects.
New Business: Student Trips (taken out of order)
Agenda Order
Discussion Summary
Chair Mancuso moved to take items 12.4 and 12.5 first. A short recess would follow, so members could read materials sent that evening by Dr. Brian Mazjanis, Assistant Superintendent for Finance.
Key Decisions

Approved by a show of hands; the Chair counted five in favor. Moved by Chair Andrea Mancuso, seconded by Vice Chair Katy Rice. How the other two members voted was not stated on the recording. [1:09:22]
12.4 — Chamber Singers Overnight Trip, April 2027 (packet pages 43–45)
Discussion Summary

About 30 students and at least 11 adults plan a trip over April 2027 vacation. The cost is capped at $800 per person. New York City and Philadelphia are the leading choices. Nashville was ruled out because group flights were too expensive.

Cavallaro asked how students with less money can take part [1:10:04]. Proulx said students earn credit toward their own cost by the work they put into fundraisers. Events include a swing concert and silent auction on Dec. 12 and a cabaret dinner on Jan. 29.
Key Decisions
Approved, first and final approval, by a show of hands. Moved by Vice Chair Katy Rice, seconded by Brooke Reed. All seven members voted yes; the two student representatives gave advisory yes votes.
12.5 — Middle School Travel Club Trip to Greece, Spring 2027 (packet pages 46–50)
Discussion Summary

Three to five students and two or three parents would join an EF Educational Tours trip to Greece over April 2027 vacation. The packet says the district pays nothing; families pay most of the cost and the club will fundraise.

Cavallaro said the trip likely costs much more than $800 per student. She asked that the district keep equity and access in mind. A staff member said the middle school will help the trip leader find fundraising, but plans aren't set yet.
Key Decisions

Approved, first and final approval, by a show of hands. Moved by Vice Chair Katy Rice, seconded by Allison Brunette. All seven members voted yes; the two student representatives gave advisory yes votes.
The committee then took a short recess [1:23:36].
Old Business
11.1 — Fire Alarm Phase 1 Replacement, Final Approval (packet page 30)
Discussion Summary

This emergency spending replaces the first phase of the 1988 fire alarm system shared by Westbrook High School and the vocational center. It got first approval on Oct. 14, when the cost was given as $38,650 from contingency, the budget's fund for unexpected costs. There was no discussion.
Key Decisions
Final approval, 7–0. Moved by Erin Cavallaro, seconded by Noreen Poitras.
11.2 — Energy Efficiency Phase 2 (Siemens), Tabled (packet page 31)
Discussion Summary

This item would let Siemens design a next round of energy projects. It got first approval on Oct. 14. Under the agreement, the district pays about $146,000 only if it goes ahead with none of the projects. If it goes ahead, that cost is folded into the project.

Chair Mancuso said the rush had been to meet a year-end funding deadline. At a meeting with the City and Siemens earlier that week, she learned that deadline could no longer be met [1:28:45]. Staff confirmed the district missed the window for Efficiency Maine incentive money this year. A staff member said more may be available next year, but the amount isn't known.

Members asked how bids work and who owns the plans. A staff member said the district sees every vendor's price, though Siemens picks the bidders. Reading the agreement, Mancuso said the plans become the district's once it pays the fee or orders project work.

Mancuso raised timing [1:44:06]. Siemens has up to 120 days to deliver its plans. The district then has 30 days to order project work or owe the fee. That could mean paying an unbudgeted fee this fiscal year, from a small contingency fund.
“I just want to be careful about what we're saying here. In FY28, this will not be budget neutral. It will be budget neutral over the term of the loan.”

The same speaker said the projects are ones the district will need anyway. They added that Siemens' first-phase projects came in on or under budget, and that the district's lawyer had reviewed the agreement.

“I was supportive of moving forward with this PDA at our last meeting in large part because I and I think others were operating under the understanding that we would potentially have access to ... approximately $1 million of Efficiency Maine funding ... I think for me that materially changes the financial picture ... I'm not suggesting by any means that we abandon the project, but I do think we have a responsibility to fully understand the funding landscape and the potential impact on our budget, on taxpayers.”

Mancuso suggested tabling the item, or setting it aside, until early 2027, possibly with a special meeting where Siemens presents again. Members agreed. Cavallaro said she was disappointed the funding was missed.
Key Decisions
Tabled until the committee has more information on how the projects could be paid for, 7–0. Moved by Erin Cavallaro, seconded by Noreen Poitras. A tabled item can be brought back by a later motion.
New Business
12.1.1 — Half-Time Physical Science Teacher, Westbrook High School (packet page 32)
Discussion Summary

Derek Pelletier was nominated for a half-time science post. The packet lists his pay as $30,554, which is half of $61,108, pro-rated from his start date. He is now a long-term substitute at the high school. The Chair asked for first and final approval because of the substitute shortage.
Key Decisions
Approved, first and final approval, 7–0. Moved by Dr. Flynn Ross, seconded by Noreen Poitras.
12.2 — Policy KLGC: Immigration Enforcement at Schools (packet pages 33–36)

“The intent of the policy is to ensure that the Westbrook School Department schools and educational programs remain safe and accessible to all students and staff regardless of immigration status by limiting, to the fullest extent possible, consistent with state and federal law, voluntary consent for entry into nonpublic areas of the facility by law enforcement officers for immigration enforcement purposes, and limiting consent to disclosure of protected records held by the school to law enforcement officers for immigration enforcement purposes.”
Discussion Summary

Chair Mancuso said state law now requires this policy. It must be in place within 90 days of the Maine Attorney General's guidance, issued at the end of September. The policy follows a model from the Maine School Management Association.

Cavallaro explained it at Poitras's request [2:01:14]. Staff may not, on their own, let officers into private areas of a school, or give them student records, for immigration enforcement. Officers must show a court-issued warrant, and a designated administrator reviews it first.
Asked about the school resource officers [2:04:03], Cavallaro said the policy doesn't cover them. The Chair said the policy puts into writing guidance staff have followed for over a year.
Key Decisions
Adopted, first and final approval, by a show of hands. Moved by Erin Cavallaro, seconded by Brooke Reed. All seven members voted yes; the two student representatives gave advisory yes votes.
12.3 — Contract with Great Schools Partnership (packet pages 37–42)
Discussion Summary

The contract pays Great Schools Partnership up to $31,000 for 20 days of work on the special education review, from Sept. 15, 2026 to March 31, 2028. It is paid in four payments: three of $7,750 and a last one of $7,740 (packet page 41).
Dr. Lancia said a parent meeting is set for Tuesday, Dec. 1, from 5 to 6 PM [2:08:30]. Initial findings are hoped for in January.

The first two payments would come from an unspent grant from the Mid-Atlantic Equity Consortium [2:11:17]. Lancia said the grant has been on the books for about three years, and its terms were broad. Cavallaro said a quick search suggested the money came in March 2021. The Chair asked that the June agenda include how the last two payments will be paid.
Cavallaro asked again for a full list of the district's grants. Dr. Mazjanis said it would come to the next Finance Committee meeting.
Key Decisions

First approval. Moved by Vice Chair Katy Rice, seconded by Brooke Reed. All seven members voted yes; the two student representatives gave advisory yes votes. The Chair kept it to first approval because it involves funding. It returns for final approval later.
12.6 — $6,385.10 from Contingency for Solar Project Costs (packet page 51)
Discussion Summary

Late in the project, lawyers said the solar project needed a performance bond, which protects against a contractor failing to finish the job. It cost $90,417. Waived electric company connection fees saved $37,823, leaving a $52,594 gap. Interest earned on the borrowed bond money covers $46,208.90, and contingency covers the remaining $6,385.10.
Chair Mancuso asked how this came up so late [2:20:17]. Dr. Mazjanis said he felt the same way. He said the project is now closed out.

Mazjanis said a federal tax credit for the solar project, hoped to exceed $768,000, is being pursued. He said it could arrive in late winter or early spring, but shouldn't be counted until it is in hand [2:29:34].
Key Decisions
First approval, 7–0. Moved by Erin Cavallaro, seconded by Dr. Flynn Ross. It returns in December for final approval.
12.7 — $11,450.76 from Contingency for Canal and Congin Bathrooms (packet page 52)
Discussion Summary
The Canal and Congin bathroom project ran $54,064.50 over budget. Bond money (called “bond revenue” at the meeting) covers $42,613.74, and contingency covers $11,450.76.

Cavallaro asked why the committee heard about $94,000 last month [2:32:35]. A staff member said that was the worst case before the final bills came in. Bids came in higher than expected, and a late bill in September showed the overrun.
Cavallaro raised concern that the committee learned of it so late, when the project was nearly done. She asked whether better notice rules are needed [2:38:35].

A staff member said the team has talked about reviewing risks after each bid and meeting more often on spending. Cavallaro noted that keeping $250,000 that had been moved from this bond to the solar project would have covered the gap. The staff member agreed and said future bonds should include about a 10% cushion.
Key Decisions
First approval, 7–0. Moved by Erin Cavallaro, seconded by Dr. Flynn Ross. It returns in December for final approval.
Closing
Dates, Public Comment & Adjournment
Discussion Summary

Upcoming meetings: Educational Programs Committee, Dec. 9 at 5 PM at Central Office; School Committee, Dec. 9 at 7 PM in Room 114 at the high school; Policy Committee, Dec. 16 at 5 PM at Central Office. No one spoke during the second public comment period.
Key Decisions
Adjourned, 7–0. Moved by Noreen Poitras, seconded by Vice Chair Katy Rice. The clock time was not stated on the recording.

howMade: This summary was produced from the meeting video (linked above, hosted on the City's Vimeo showcase). The audio was transcribed with AI-assisted speech-to-text and speaker identification. This process cross-checked names against the School Committee roster and the agenda packet, attributed speakers from context (introductions, roll-call order, direct address by the Chair) rather than the raw diarization labels alone, and drafted this summary and the quoted excerpts. Quotes are lightly cleaned of filler words/false starts but not reworded. A separate AI accuracy check compared this summary with the transcript and agenda packet, and errors it found were corrected. The Westbrook Currents editor then read it and checked key points against the meeting video. Westbrook Currents is independent. The Westbrook School Department did not review or approve this summary.
